names.summary: A 212-byte beacon frame from a cubesat (key LASP:len212). Only a frame sequence counter and an on-board clock were located by the engine, so the rest of the frame is unidentified. The clock is a seconds counter on a J2000-style epoch.

fields.name: frame_sequence_counter
fields.rationale: u2be that increases almost always (frac_up 0.996) and wraps 9 times in 4.6 days, which is typical of a 16-bit sequence number. The rate of 0.0048 per second is the average over the observation gaps, not the true rate. The sun/shadow correlations are weak and not meaningful. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: onboard_clock_seconds
fields.rationale: u4be that rises at exactly 1.0 per second with no resets, so it is a seconds clock. The epoch offset points to J2000. The power_bus hint and narrow band are artifacts of a monotonic counter and should be ignored. [3/3 samples agree]

names.health: Not enough evidence for battery or thermal health since no such fields were identified. The clock shows no resets in the window, so there is no sign of a reboot. The 9 wraps of the 16-bit counter are consistent with normal wrapping by design.

names.summary: A 248-byte housekeeping frame with a header sequence counter, several redundant time/uptime counters, and a large block of power telemetry: many solar-panel or channel currents that drop to near zero in shadow, battery voltage and state-of-charge fields that follow sunlight with a lag, and signed currents. Every frame has an eclipse in the previous 80 minutes, so the lagged correlations reflect real physics.

fields.name: frame_sequence_counter
fields.rationale: u2 counter that increases about 0.004/s with 9 wraps or resets. It has no sun dependence, so it is likely a frame or beacon sequence number. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: obc_unix_time_j2000
fields.rationale: Increases at exactly 1 s/s, with a J2000-like epoch offset and no resets. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: uptime_or_secondary_clock
fields.rationale: Ticks at 1 s/s and moves with the clock at offset 6, so a second time base such as uptime. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: rolling_counter_a
fields.rationale: u2 counter at 0.081/s with 6 wraps. It has the same rate and wraps as offset 74, so the two are probably paired counters. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: slow_counter_u2
fields.rationale: Increments by about 1 per 2500 s (0.0004/s) and has the same rate as offset 38, so a slow tick counter or a low-order copy of it. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: slow_counter_u4
fields.rationale: Monotonic at 0.0004/s, mirroring offset 34, so a slow event or time-tick counter. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: event_counter
fields.rationale: Monotonic u4 at 0.153/s with no resets, so a cumulative operation or event count. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: cumulative_counter_fast
fields.rationale: Monotonic u4 at 1.2/s with no resets, tracking the clocks, so possibly a tick or cycle counter. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: rolling_counter_b
fields.rationale: Same rate and 6 wraps as offset 32, offset by a constant, so a paired counter. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: temperature_a
fields.rationale: u1 in the range 65-84 that is higher in shadow and moves with offset 85. The values are narrow and only weakly sun-correlated. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: temperature_b
fields.rationale: Tracks offset 83 with a constant offset and the same orbit-linked behavior. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_temperature
fields.rationale: Narrow range, rises in sun and falls in shadow, with a long time constant (tau 80 min or more). That fits an internal or battery temperature. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_voltage_a
fields.rationale: Narrow range of 1766-2258 that is higher in sun, with a shadow/sun ratio of 0.82. It correlates with the offset 90 group. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_voltage_b
fields.rationale: Smooth, narrow-range (spread 0.21) and rises in sun and falls in shadow. The lag correlation is 0.97 and it groups with the other battery fields. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_current_1
fields.rationale: Near zero in shadow and about 100 in sun, with rho_sun of 0.915. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_or_bus_voltage_raw
fields.rationale: Narrow range of 16312-16776, a few percent lower in shadow, and it follows sunlight with a lag. [2/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_current_2
fields.rationale: Zero in shadow and about 60-70 in sun, and it tracks offset 93. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_panel_power_1
fields.rationale: Near zero in shadow (ratio 0.014) and about 21000 in sun. The solar-input hint is consistent with this. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_current_3
fields.rationale: u1 that is 0 in shadow and about 19 in sun, with rho_sun of 0.926. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_panel_power_2
fields.rationale: Near zero in shadow and about 20000 in sun, parallel to offsets 98 and 114. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_current_4
fields.rationale: Zero in shadow and a plateau of about 27 in sun, with no trend, so it is set directly by illumination. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_panel_power_3
fields.rationale: Near zero in shadow and about 19000 in sun. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_or_charge_value_f32
fields.rationale: f32 that ranges from 1.4 to 18, higher in sun and decaying in shadow. It could be charge power or voltage. [2/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_cell_voltage_a
fields.rationale: Smooth, lag correlation 0.98 at tau 40 min, rising in sun and falling in shadow. It moves with offset 126, so a battery-related group. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_cell_voltage_b
fields.rationale: Same smooth lagged behavior as offset 124 (lag correlation 0.978), so it belongs to the same battery group. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_current
fields.rationale: Signed, positive in sun (about 90) and negative in shadow (about -170), so a charge/discharge current. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_state_of_charge
fields.rationale: Confined to 95-100, follows sunlight with tau 40 min, and moves with the battery voltages. That matches a state of charge in percent. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_panel_power_4
fields.rationale: Near zero in shadow, about 19000 in sun, and same family as 98. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_panel_power_5
fields.rationale: Near zero in shadow, about 20000 in sun. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: solar_panel_power_6
fields.rationale: Near zero in shadow, about 22000 in sun. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_energy_or_capacity
fields.rationale: u3 lagged with tau of 80 min (rho 0.9). It rises in sun and falls in shadow, so it is probably an integrated battery energy or capacity value. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_current_2
fields.rationale: Signed, positive in sun and negative in shadow, so a charge/discharge current. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: charge_current_signed
fields.rationale: Signed, about +570 in sun and a constant -5203 in shadow. The saturated shadow value suggests a clamped discharge reading. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: load_or_charge_current_negative
fields.rationale: Zero in shadow and negative in sun (about -300), so a sign-inverted charge or sun-dependent current. The bus hint is weak. [2/3 samples agree]

fields.name: charge_status_signed_byte
fields.rationale: Signed byte with only 8 distinct values, a flat -16 in shadow and about 12 in sun, so likely a coarse current or mode value. [2/3 samples agree]

fields.name: sun_gated_value
fields.rationale: Zero in shadow and variable in sun, with a range of 0-250. There is not enough evidence to name it. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: battery_energy_wh_counter
fields.rationale: Lagged with tau of 80 min (rho 0.93) and a shadow/sun ratio of 0.76. It moves with offset 162, so it is an integrating battery quantity. [3/3 samples agree]

names.health: The field names point to roughly nine sequence-counter wraps in 4.6 days, but a 2-byte sequence number wraps by design, so this is not evidence of reboots. The clocks show no resets. The battery fields follow the sun/shadow cycle normally with a state of charge of 95-100%, so there is no sign of trouble, but 4.6 days is too short to judge ageing.

names.summary: An 84-byte housekeeping-style beacon with a 16-bit wrapping sequence counter, a 32-bit wall-clock timestamp, and a 24-bit uptime-like counter. Only counters and clocks were located; no sensor channels were identified.

fields.name: frame_sequence_counter
fields.rationale: u2be that only increases and wraps (8 resets) at about 0.0044 per second, i.e. one tick per ~228 s on average. This is most likely a sequence counter that increments per frame or per beacon type, and it wraps by design. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: obc_time_seconds_j2000
fields.rationale: u4be rising exactly 1.0 per second with no resets. The epoch guess is J2000 with an offset of about 946684766 s, so it is probably an onboard clock in seconds. [3/3 samples agree]

fields.name: uptime_counter_200ms
fields.rationale: u3be rising at 5.0 per second with no resets, and it moves in lockstep with the clock at offset 6. This looks like an uptime or tick counter at 5 Hz (0.2 s per tick). Its minimum of 1.27M ticks is about 70 h since boot at the start of the window. [3/3 samples agree]

names.health: No reboots are seen in the window: the 5 Hz uptime counter never reset and the clock ran monotonically. The sequence counter wrapped 8 times, but that is by design. There are no battery or thermal fields, so there is not enough evidence for any other health assessment.
